rationale: Successor to the removed-leader experiment with a changed basis: the harness now adds an external-trigger phase after the fixed progress window in which an eligible voter campaigns explicitly (the MsgHup path a forced election or operator action uses) and the harness then proposes on whichever eligible node takes leadership. The two original comparisons are retained so the successor re-measures the same predicates on the new basis, and a third comparison records the enclosing boundary honestly: the stall ends once an eligible voter is told to campaign, so the observed nonprogress is about the absence of any internal trigger, not about a permanently broken cluster.

scope.description: Two probes on freshly elected three-voter clusters, each proposing, replicating and applying a ConfChangeV2 that removes node 1, running a fixed 80-round progress window with round-robin ticking and prompt delivery, probing the read path on the ineligible leader, and then, for the probe without step-down, letting an eligible voter campaign explicitly and proposing on the resulting leader.
assumptions: The removal is proposed and replicated by the real producer path and applied only after it is committed, with each node's applied index advanced as an application does.
Timers are driven by ticking each node once per round in a fixed order with messages delivered immediately after each tick.

The external trigger is one MsgHup stepped into follower 2, which is the same message Node.Campaign and a forced election use; the harness then proposes one write on whichever eligible node becomes leader.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no restart, snapshot, partition, joint configuration or operator-side membership change is simulated.
The initial configuration is {1,2,3}; after the removal it is {2,3} with quorum 2 and node 1 is a non-voter.
excluded: Joint configurations, learners, multi-node atomic changes and demotion of the leader
The embedding application's membership controller and its operator interfaces
Any claim about how quickly an operator would notice or act in a real deployment

experiment.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). assuranceClusterWithConfig builds {1,2,3} through newNetworkWithConfig so the step-down control uses the real Config, elects node 1, asserts StateLeader and advances the applied index. Each probe marshals ConfChangeV2{RemoveNode 1}, steps it as a MsgProp into the leader, drives the produced messages until the cluster quiesces and checks that the proposed index committed; every node whose committed index covers it runs the documented type-based apply loop and then advances its applied index. The probe emits removal_applied, issues one proposal on the leader and one on follower 2 (delivering the forwarded MsgProp to the leader) and emits progress_setup with probe_id, step_down_on_removal, ticks, leader state, configuration membership, voters, last index and committed index. It then runs the fixed progress window (each node ticked once per round in a fixed order, its messages delivered immediately) and emits progress_window with the proposal errors, forwarding operands, last index and committed index before/after, node states, whether an eligible node holds leadership, the followers' election timers and any undelivered messages. For the probe without step-down it then forwards a ReadIndex from follower 2 into the leader, delivers the heartbeats to the real followers, steps exactly one acknowledgment and then the remaining ones, and emits two removed_leader_read events with acks_from_current_voters and read_answers. Finally it emits trigger_setup, steps a single MsgHup into follower 2, runs a further fixed window of ticks with prompt delivery, proposes one write on whichever eligible node is leader by then, and emits post_trigger_progress with new_leader_id, new_leader_elected, proposal_committed, the last index before that proposal, all node states and any undelivered messages.
experiment.responsibility: A cluster whose configuration no longer contains its current leader owns reaching a configuration-consistent leader so that client writes can commit again, while an eligible voter that is explicitly told to campaign is expected to be able to take leadership and commit. The experiment measures both sides: the absence of an internal trigger leaves the cluster stalled, and an external trigger ends the stall.

comparisons.description: With StepDownOnRemoval false, the cluster elects a new leader inside the fixed progress window without any external trigger.
Control: with StepDownOnRemoval true the same sequence elects a new leader inside the same window.
Boundary control: once an eligible voter is explicitly told to campaign, an eligible node takes leadership and a subsequent proposal commits.

experiment.revision_reason: Changed basis: the harness adds a post-window external-trigger phase (explicit MsgHup on an eligible voter followed by a proposal on the new leader) and a third comparison for it, so the same two progress predicates are re-measured together with the boundary of the stall.
